chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah from someone else from Aban ibn Uthman from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the Words of Allah the Exalted: 'Then when they fall down by the side'
He said: 'When it falls upon the ground, so eat from it, and feed the contented one and the passer-by.'

He said: 'The contented one is the one who is pleased with what is given to him and does not get angry, nor frowns, nor twists his jaw in anger; and the passer-by is the one who passes by you so that you feed him.'

key_terms.الْقَانِعُ: the contented one (who accepts charity without anger or frowning)
key_terms.الْمُعْتَرُّ: the passer-by (one who passes by and is fed)
key_terms.جُنُوبُهَا: their sides (referring to the sacrificial animal falling on its side)

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'when they fall by the side' in the context of sacrificial animals?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the practical application of Surah Al-Hajj 22:36, defining the 'falling' of the sacrificial animal as the moment it settles on the ground after slaughter, thereby permitting consumption. It further distinguishes two categories of charity recipients: the 'Qa'in', who is content and does not complain, and the 'Mu'tarr', a passer-by who is fed opportunistically as they pass, reflecting the Shia emphasis on dignified and situational charity distribution.

en.hubeali:
Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Sama’at, from someone else, from Aban Bin Usman, from Abdul Rahman Bin Abu Abdullah, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>
regarding the Words of Allahazwj the Exalted. [22:36] then when they fall down by the side.
He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When it falls upon the ground, so eat from it, and feed the needy who do not beg, and the passer-by’.

He (the narrator) said: ‘الْقَانِعُ is the one who is pleased with what he is given and neither gets angry nor frown, nor twists his mouth out of anger; and الْمُعْتَرُّ is the one who passes by, so you feed him’.
en.sarwar: 2. Humayd ibn Ziyad has narrated from ibn Sama‘ah from more than one person from Aban ibn ‘Uthman from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn abu ‘Abd Allah who has said the following:
“This is about the words of Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, ‘When their sides reach the ground.’ [22:36]
Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that it means when they fall on the ground. ‘. . . use it for food and feed thereof to those contented and those who ask.’ [22:36]
He (the Imam) said that al-Qani‘ are those who become gratified, do not become angry, frown or twist the corner of their mouths out of anger and al-Mu‘tar is one who passes by so you feed him.’”
